messages:
maria_s: Hey, running into a weird AccessDenied from KMS when decrypting envelopes across accounts. SDK error: "AccessDeniedException: User is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt". Same role can decrypt in the source account, but when we assume the cross-account role it fails.

kevin_iam: can you paste the decrypt call and the CMK ARN? usually it's either grant-token missing or key policy not allowing the assumed role principal.

maria_s: CMK arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111111111111:key/abcd-ef01. We create a grant from account 111111... to role arn:aws:iam::222222222222:role/redwood-data-access, then the service in account 222 calls sts:AssumeRole and tries to decrypt. Grant list shows the grant exists.

maria_s: log snippet:
```
KMSException: AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::222222222222:assumed-role/redwood-data-access/session is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111111111111:key/abcd-ef01
```

kevin_iam: two quick checks: (1) confirm the decrypt call includes the grant token if you created the grant in the same request window; (2) check encryption context mismatch. If the data key was encrypted with an encryptionContext, decrypt requires the same context.

jon_eng: also ensure the key policy explicitly allows the grantee principal (the assumed-role principal ARN or the role ARN) to use the key. Grants are separate, but a key policy can still block. Example minimal key policy addition: 
```json
{"Sid":"AllowCrossAccountRole","Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::222222222222:role/redwood-data-access"},"Action":["kms:Decrypt","kms:DescribeKey"],"Resource":"*"}
```

kevin_iam: small correction: the Principal should be in the Key policy root-level statement (not under Resource). And for cross-account grants you can create a grant with GranteePrincipal set to the role ARN. If you did the grant in account 111 and the process in 222 assumes the role, you still must either (A) pass the grant token returned by CreateGrant to the decrypt call, or (B) have the key policy allow the role. Grants are not magically visible to the assumed session unless you use the grant token.

charles_oncall: we hit this before: our flow created the grant, then the role assumed immediately; SDKs sometimes don't forward the grant token. You can confirm by running: 
```bash
aws kms list-grants --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111111111111:key/abcd-ef01 --profile owner-account
```
and if you need the token from create-grant: 
```bash
aws kms create-grant --key-id <key> --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::222222222222:role/redwood-data-access --operations Decrypt --query GrantToken --output text
```

maria_s: we do see the grant in list-grants, but create-grant was done by a human and not wired into the deploy process. The service in account 222 never got a grant token. Should we rotate to a key policy change instead?

kevin_iam: for durable cross-account access, prefer key policy that references the role ARN (or account principal) rather than ephemeral grants. Grants are useful for short-lived ad-hoc access or when you need to delegate without changing key policy. If you go policy route, be explicit with conditions like aws:PrincipalArn. Example: 
```json
{"Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::222222222222:role/redwood-data-access"},"Action":["kms:Decrypt"],"Resource":"*","Condition":{"StringEquals":{"aws:PrincipalArn":"arn:aws:iam::222222222222:role/redwood-data-access"}}}
```

jon_eng: also watch for aws:SourceAccount/sourceVpce and kms:ViaService conditions. If the key policy has SourceAccount restriction, cross-account assume-role flows can get rejected.

maria_s: good call — the key policy had a SourceAccount condition locking to 111111111111, which blocked the assumed principal (sts:assumed-role ARNs have different account scoping). I removed that condition for the Decrypt statement and deployed a test.

kms-bot: deploy-bot triggered: policy update applied to key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111111111111:key/abcd-ef01 by maria_s at 2026-03-19T21:05:00Z

maria_s: test results: decrypt now succeeds from account 222 after assuming role. Thanks! A couple notes for the runbook: avoid relying on grant tokens for automated cross-account services unless the token is propagated by the service. Prefer explicit key policy entries for known roles. Also include troubleshooting steps: list-grants, get-key-policy, verify encryptionContext.

kevin_iam: adding: when using envelope encryption across accounts, ensure the encrypting service included the same encryption context fields (if any). Different contexts = decrypt denied even if policy allows.

charles_oncall: I'll add an item to the incident runbook about prefer-key-policy and a snippet for our standard cross-account key policy template.

maria_s: will also add the exact aws cli commands we used to the KB. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
